quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim
rationale: Vendor gives a full IP indemnity plus indemnities for breach of law, data breach, bodily injury and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard procedure and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies; Customer's indemnity is appropriately narrow.

quote: Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables
rationale: Customer owns Customer Data and Deliverables, Vendor retains only its pre-existing technology with a perpetual licence back, and joint ownership is excluded.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have re-based the cap on all fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months (with a USD 1,000,000 floor), because "Fees" as defined is only the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, which would leave us with no meaningful recourse. Indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement remain outside the cap per Section 21.3.

ops.newText: shall not exceed the greater of (a) all fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000
ops.oldText: shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim

proposal.summary: The cap is illusory: "Fees" is defined in Section 1.5 as only the Implementation Fee (USD 12,000), and the cap is further limited to the first Order Form. Our position is a mutual cap of the greater of 12 months' fees actually paid or payable across the Agreement and USD 1,000,000. Mutuality, damages exclusions and Excluded Claims in 21.2–21.3 are acceptable as drafted.

quote: shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim
rationale: The cap is illusory: "Fees" is defined in Section 1.5 as only the Implementation Fee (USD 12,000), and the cap is further limited to the first Order Form. Our position is a mutual cap of the greater of 12 months' fees actually paid or payable across the Agreement and USD 1,000,000. Mutuality, damages exclusions and Excluded Claims in 21.2–21.3 are acceptable as drafted.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.
rationale: Customer may assign to affiliates/successors without consent, Vendor needs our consent and may not assign to a competitor, and no change-of-control trigger exists against us.

quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation is imposed on Customer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced the liquidated-damages charge with customary late interest. Our position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; a 15% weekly charge is punitive and inconsistent with the good-faith dispute right in Section 7.3.

ops.newText: If any undisputed invoice is not paid within thirty days of its due date, Vendor may charge interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month and the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, which is Vendor's sole remedy for late payment.
ops.oldText: If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

proposal.summary: We do not accept liquidated damages payable by Customer; 15% of annual Fees per week is punitive and likely unenforceable. Standard late interest is the appropriate remedy, and it should not apply to amounts disputed in good faith under Section 7.3.

quote: Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid
rationale: We do not accept liquidated damages payable by Customer; 15% of annual Fees per week is punitive and likely unenforceable. Standard late interest is the appropriate remedy, and it should not apply to amounts disputed in good faith under Section 7.3.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right
rationale: Affiliates and contractors are covered, paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable, transfer to successors is permitted and revocation is limited to uncured material breach.

quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service
rationale: No non-compete binds Customer; the restriction in 12.4 binds Vendor only, which is acceptable to us.

quote: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
rationale: Customer has a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund and no termination fee; Vendor has no convenience right. Matches our preferred position.

quote: no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice
rationale: Frequency, notice, off-site independent auditor, Vendor-borne cost subject to a 5% underpayment threshold and no direct system access all match our preferred position.

quote: governed by the laws of the State of New York
rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County courts and no arbitration; our preferred position.

quote: Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.
rationale: The MFN runs in Customer's favour, which we welcome; no redline required.

quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies.
rationale: No take-or-pay or shortfall exposure; fees are payable only for ordered Services.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: hiring any person who responds to general recruitment
rationale: No non-solicit or no-hire restriction binds Customer.

quote: renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal
rationale: 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% meet our preferred position.

quote: provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form
rationale: Six months' transition assistance, 30-day machine-readable data return with no fee-dispute hostage-taking, and certified deletion meet our preferred position.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria.
rationale: Professional-services warranty, 90-day deliverable conformance (hosted Services for the full term), no-malicious-code and compliance warranties, with re-perform/repair/replace/refund remedies not swallowed by the disclaimer.

quote: professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000
rationale: Coverage lines and limits meet our preferred position, with certificates on request and no limitation of Vendor's liability.
